title: Rapid candidate rescue: 7-day hire playbook
content:
Overview:
This playbook is a short-form, operational runbook to convert a high-priority open headcount into an accepted offer within 7 calendar days. It's intended for roles where time-to-fill materially impacts product delivery, launch readiness, or contractual obligations (e.g., Dedicated infra capacity rollout).

When to trigger:
- Hiring owner (PM/Eng manager) flags a role as critical and requests a <7-day fill.
- Candidate in offer ladder stalls or offer declined and immediate backfill is required.
- Exec/Customer commitment tied to headcount delivery.

Primary goals:
- 7-day SLA from trigger -> signed offer (stretch target).
- Maintain hire quality: use an accelerated but defensible rubric and panel.
- Provide a shallow but consistent onboarding checklist so new hire can contribute within first 10 business days.

Triage checklist (first 6 hours):
1) Confirm scope: hiring manager writes 3 must-have skills and 2 nice-to-have skills.
2) Identify fallback pool: internal transfers, contractors with conversion potential, boomerang candidates.
3) Assign stakeholders: Recruiter (owner), Hiring manager (decision owner), People Ops (comp/offer), Interviewer lead (panel coordinator).
4) Decide interview format: 60–90m micro-panel (combined screen + deep dive) or parallel 30m slices (speed-loop).
5) Reserve offer authority: pre-approve comp band or escalation path to enable same-day offers.

Day-by-day timeline (7-day plan):
Day 0 (trigger): kickoff email, update req, post internal ping to fallback pool, open first outreach batch.
Day 1: Screen 6 shortlisted candidates (phone/VC 20–30m). Identify top 2–3 for extended interviews.
Day 2: Schedule micro-panels for top candidates; blocker calendar holds for panelists.
Day 3: Conduct panels; collect rubric scores within 4 hours of interview.
Day 4: Manager decision meeting, reference checks initiated, comp approved.
Day 5: Draft offer and proposed start date; get verbal pre-approval from candidate if still engaged.
Day 6: Offer sent (email + call). Follow up immediately if unanswered.
Day 7: Close (acceptance or fallback plan executed). If accepted, start rapid onboarding prep.

Panel structure (recommended):
- 15m: Context + role expectations (manager)
- 30–40m: Technical deep-dive or case (engineer/product)
- 15m: Collaboration/culture fit + behavioural probes (people ops or peer)
- 10m: Candidate Q&A and next steps

Accelerated interview rubric (single sheet anchors, 1–5):
- Technical competence (core skills): 5 = obvious expert, 3 = solid practical, 1 = missing fundamentals.
- Product & system judgment (tradeoffs, design): 5 = clear, structured answers with alternatives; 3 = reasonable; 1 = weak tradeoffs.
- Collaboration and communication: 5 = concise, gives examples of cross-team delivery; 3 = OK; 1 = poor.
- Learning & ramp potential: 5 = fast learner with evidence; 3 = average; 1 = low.
- Role-fit urgency multiplier: +1 if candidate has immediate relevant experience (reduces onboarding time).
Decision rule: average score >=3.8 -> strong recommend; 3.0–3.79 -> conditional recommend (manager to weigh); <3.0 -> no go. Reference checks should address any borderline areas before offer.

Offer cadence and negotiation guidance:
- Pre-approve one stretch comp authority for emergency hires (documented in req).
- Start with P50+ band if candidate meets most must-haves; include one-time sign-on if relocation or counter-offer risk.
- Use 48-hour standard response window; escalate to manager after 24 hours if no reply.
- Keep negotiations tight: one counter-offer allowed, then final sign-off required.

Fallback and failover plan:
- If top candidate declines, immediately move to next in pipeline (Day 6–7).
- If pipeline exhausted, convert internal contractor or open a 14-day extended search with 'warm handoff' to hiring manager and recruiter for weekly check-ins.

Rapid onboarding (first 10 business days checklist):
Pre-boarding (before Day 0 of new hire):
- Account provisioning checklist sent to IT with expected start date.
- Manager writes first-week 3 deliverables (small, measurable).
- Peer buddy assigned and calendar invites sent for week 1 syncs.

Week 1 (day 1–5):
- Day 1: 30m manager welcome, 60m team intro, systems access verification.
- Day 2: Setup dev environment (pair session with buddy), assign first microtask.
- Day 3: Review codebase/architecture overview (peer-led).
- Day 4: Shadow production run or runbook exercise.
- Day 5: First micro-deliverable review + feedback loop.

Week 2 (day 6–10):
- Start contributing to a small bug/feature with mentor. Weekly syncs with manager.
- 1:1 review at end of week 2 to calibrate ramp plan.

Communication templates (short):
- Kickoff email subject: "Rapid-hire kickoff: [Role] — 7-day SLA"
- Panel invite copy: short context, timebox, key evaluation areas.
- Offer subject: "Redwood Inference — Offer for [Role]: [Level]" (attach 1-page comp summary).

Quick escalation RACI (high level):
- Recruiter: owner (day-to-day candidate sourcing and comms).
- Hiring manager: decision owner (final say on hire).
- People Ops: comp/offer + compliance.
- Interviewer lead: ensures rubric completeness and score submission.

Common risks & mitigations:
- Candidate ghosting: Mitigate by immediate scheduling and multiple contact channels; use recruiter+manager outreach.
- Quality drop: Track rubric distributions; refuse to skip core technical screen unless manager signs risk waiver.
- Offer approval lag: Pre-authorize fallback comp and emergency escalation path to VP People (documented).

Post-mortem: If SLA not met, standard retrospective template: root causes, time spent at each stage, leak points (sourcing, scheduling, approvals), and recommended permanent changes (e.g., maintain a small bench of approved contractor-to-perm conversions).

Why this is different from standard hires:
- Time-compressed decisions require explicit pre-approvals and a well-defined fallback pool.
- We favour structured micro-panels over long, multi-stage loops to reduce candidate fatigue and scheduling latency.

Notes to people ops team (practical):
- Keep a live "rapid-rescue" spreadsheet with 10 warm leads per priority role.
- Rotate a 2-week on-call recruiter who owns the next 7-day SLA hires.
- Maintain a 1-pager with pre-approved comp flex for emergency use (tracked in Confluence).

Attachments & links (in this doc):
- Rapid offer email template (confluence link)
- Short reference check script (confluence link)
- Emergency comp approval form (JIRA ticket template)

Open questions / future iterations:
- Should we widen to 14-day SLA for senior ICs where multiple stakeholder loops are mandatory?
- Can we pilot a dedicated 48-hour interview window each week where hiring managers reserve time for rapid panels?

-- End of playbook --
